topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture on cancer therapy and outlines the core learning objectives.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss standard modalities of cancer treatment—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with their toxicities and efflux pump-mediated resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting cellular vulnerabilities, checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic tumor vulnerabilities, including hormone dependence, defective cell cycle checkpoints, and synthetic lethality in DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Oncogene-targeted therapies and kinase inhibitor resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine targeted inhibition of hyperactive oncogenic kinases and the subsequent emergence of resistance, bypass pathways, and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the use of engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates to target cell surface receptors and selectively deliver cytotoxic agents.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and immune-directed strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the principles of anti-tumor immune surveillance and review immunotherapeutic approaches such as checkpoint inhibitors, BiTEs, and CAR T-cell therapy.

topics.label: Challenges, progress, and future directions in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesise historical improvements in cancer outcomes with ongoing clinical challenges, future therapeutic paradigms, and ethical dilemmas.
